language.script_notes: Both Cyrillic and Latin are used, often side by side on the same sign, with yellow signs carrying black lettering. The Cyrillic letters Ђ/ђ and Ћ/ћ appear only in this language's Street View. Chevron curve signs use black arrows on a white background.

road_furniture.bollard_color: White post with a narrow red reflector set to one side rather than in the center; almost always flat with no depth.
road_furniture.bollard_shape: Flat, slim post resembling those in Slovenia and Montenegro, but with the off-center reflector.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Only the angular thin-B guardrail profile is used, which it shares with Bosnia and Herzegovina.
road_furniture.line_paint: White center and edge lines on main roads; many rural roads are worn or unmarked.
road_furniture.curb_style: Painted kerbs in towns; open shoulders on rural roads.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Utility poles are most often round concrete or rusty metal, rounder than in Hungary or Romania. MAXI (Delhaize) supermarkets are found only here, alongside IDEA and Frikom/Jelen logos.

architecture.roof_style: Pitched tile roofs on family houses; flat roofs on the huge socialist-era blocks.
architecture.wall_construction: Family houses of red brick or plaster, very often left unfinished with exposed brick or bare concrete; enormous socialist-era concrete housing blocks and monumental brutalist civic buildings, especially in Belgrade's Novi Beograd district; Orthodox churches with domes and bell towers.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Bare red brick and grey concrete, with pastel plaster on finished houses.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Brutalist landmarks such as the Genex Tower and the Palace of the Federation; unfinished multi-storey family houses; Orthodox churches; Zastava-built cars parked outside blocks.

nature.vegetation: Sunflower and maize fields across the flat north; forested hills and fruit orchards in the center; mountain forest and limited arable land in the south.
nature.terrain: Flat Pannonian plain in the north along the Danube and Sava rivers, rolling hills in the center, and mountainous terrain in the south and east.
nature.climate_signature: Temperate continental — hot summers, cold winters, with the northern plains looking much like neighbouring Hungary.

vehicles.plate_color: White plate with black text and a blue strip on the left carrying 'SRB'.
vehicles.plate_format: Two-letter regional code, then three or four digits, separated by a shield emblem from a Cyrillic letter combination for the region.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Older Zastava cars (including the Yugo, a Yugoslav-era classic) and used Western European imports; the Street View car usually lacks the roof antenna seen on most neighbouring countries' cars.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mostly Gen 3, with the capture car usually lacking an antenna.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Good coverage of main roads and towns; occasional ferries appear on the Romanian border.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Similar flat slim bollard and black-arrow-on-white chevron signs
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The bollard's red reflector sits to one side here, always off-center; only the thin-B guardrail is used; Ђ and Ћ letters are decisive.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared thin-B guardrail, Cyrillic in one entity, similar hilly terrain and architecture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Utility poles and bollards differ; the offset red reflector and MAXI supermarkets point here.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Cyrillic script, similar Balkan architecture and farmland
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Bulgaria uses Cyrillic only on official signs, while both scripts appear side by side here; letters Ђ and Ћ appear only in Serbian.
